jobs.title: Senior Risk Program Manager - Fraud & Disputes Enablement
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the Team:

Mercury* is building a complete financial stack for startups, and Risk is how we protect our customers, Mercury, and the broader financial ecosystem. You'll join the Fraud & Disputes Enablement team, a shared-services group that makes our operations teams faster, more consistent, and ready for scrutiny. The team is made up of Quality Control, Learning & Development, and Program Management, and supports Fraud & Disputes.

Role Summary:

This is a generalist program management role for someone who builds programs from zero to one. You'll lead Mercury's Bank Charter Readiness work across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX, run the operating reviews and goal tracking that show leaders how Fraud and Disputes are performing, and use data to drive continuous improvement. You'll work with Risk Operations, Compliance, Risk Product, Engineering, Risk Strategy, and Vendor Management, and you'll show the team how AI can help us work smarter, not harder.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What You'll Do:

Lead Bank Charter Readiness

- Translate the regulatory expectations of a chartered bank (Reg E, card network rules, and the standards examiners apply) into clear, sequenced work plans owned by the right teams.

- Build Bank Charter Readiness programs from zero to one: define scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks, and report progress to executives.

- Keep teams audit-ready every day, with current SOPs, traceable decisions, defensible evidence, and clean documentation, so exam preparation never becomes a scramble.

- Coordinate responses to regulator, auditor, and partner-bank inquiries with Compliance, Legal, and Operations.

Lead Goal tracking, and Reporting for Fraud & Disputes

- Own the cadence and content of Operational Quality Reviews and Monthly CORs Reviews for Fraud and Disputes, from the data pull to the narrative to the follow-up actions.

- Define and track ops health measures and team goals, including OKRs, so leaders can see what is on track, what is at risk, and why.

- Build the reporting and dashboards leaders use to make decisions, and set up new reporting from scratch where none exists.

- Raise risks early, make trade-offs explicit, and drive decisions to closure with partners who don't report to you.

Use data for continuous improvement

- Analyze quality, productivity, and compliance data across Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX to find the patterns behind recurring problems.

- Turn those findings into durable process, tooling, and reporting improvements instead of one-off fixes.

- Work with QC, L&D, and Operations leaders to route root causes to the team that can fix them, and confirm the fix worked.

- Stand up new continuous improvement programs from zero to one and measure their results.

What You'll Bring:

- 5+ years of program management experience in risk, compliance, fraud, disputes, or operations at a bank, fintech, or other regulated financial services company.

- Banking* experience, with working knowledge of how a regulated institution runs, and direct experience working with regulators, examiners, auditors, or sponsor banks (for example exam preparation, findings remediation, or regulatory responses).

- A record of building programs from zero to one, from ambiguous problem to measurable result, with impact beyond your immediate team.

- 2+ years of experience governing BPO or other outsourced operations, with a focus on governance: SLAs, performance and quality oversight, escalations, and regular business reviews.

- Strong understanding of risk operational processes in Fraud and/or Disputes, such as case handling, investigations, chargebacks, or Reg E error resolution.

- Comfort with data: you can define metrics, build or interpret dashboards, and explain what the numbers mean.

- Experience using AI and automation to improve how work gets done, for example synthesizing evidence and documentation, drafting and maintaining SOPs, analyzing QC and vendor data, summarizing incidents, and automating status reporting.

Nice to Haves:

- Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or above) or equivalent continuous improvement experience

- ISO quality credentials (for example ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or Implementer) or a similar quality management background

- PMI certification (PMP, PgMP) or equivalent

- Experience with change management frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR, or ITIL-style incident and problem management

- Experience in QC program design, workforce management, or learning and development

- Familiarity with card network dispute rules and platforms

- Experience with Risk UX, customer-facing risk flows, in a regulated context

- Experience building and scaling a program in a high-growth environment

jobs.title: Trading Operations Lead
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
Mercury is building a complete finance stack for startups. We work hard to create the easiest and safest banking* experience possible to simplify entrepreneurs’ and business owners’ financial lives. Underneath all our products is a massive web of partners that users don’t see, requiring significant product and process investment. That’s where the Financial Partnership Operations team comes in. We work to maintain our external relationships and streamline our collective workflows to keep customers, partners, and Mercury employees happy.

We’re looking for a Trading Operations Lead to own and scale the trading operations function powering Mercury’s SEC-registered investment advisor and FINRA-member broker-dealer. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone with deep brokerage and trading operations expertise who can both set the standard for how the function operates and step directly into complex operational work when needed. This role is ideal for someone who has operated in a detail-rich, regulated environment, has strong opinions about what good trading operations looks like, communicates clearly across technical and non-technical teams, and wants the opportunity to build and evolve the function rather than simply inherit it.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

In this role, you will:

- Own the trading operations and supervisory framework, providing licensed principal oversight of order and trade activity across money market funds, mutual funds, ETFs, and fixed income; oversee operational controls, reconciliations, exceptions, and escalations, partnering closely with Engineering and Product on system-managed workflows and with our carrying broker and other investment partners to investigate issues, resolve breaks, and ensure trading activity operates within established procedures and supervisory requirements.

- Own the trade surveillance and operational control framework, including licensed supervisory review where required, oversight of pre- and post-trade controls, best execution monitoring, trade breaks and errors, escalation and remediation, and evidence that required reviews and controls are operating as designed; coordinate with Financial Crimes on surveillance alerts, suspicious activity escalations, and shared monitoring obligations.

- Own supervision of trading and order-flow reporting obligations, including CAT (all elements, including annual clock synchronization), CAIS, and TRACE, coordinating with our carrying broker and third-party reporting vendor; ensure timely and accurate compliance with SEC Rules 606 and 607 and FINRA Rule 6151, and provide supervisory review of customer account statements and trade confirmations.

- Serve as the operational escalation point for trade errors, breaks, and settlement issues, coordinating investigation and resolution across Engineering, Product, Compliance, and our carrying and executing partners, assessing customer impact, and ensuring recurring issues result in appropriate process or control improvements.

- Oversee trading-related books and records requirements, partnering with Engineering, Compliance, and our carrying broker to ensure required trade, order, allocation, and supervisory records are appropriately generated, retained, and retrievable.

- Own and maintain trading operations procedures and contribute to applicable Written Supervisory Procedures, ensuring documented controls and supervisory practices remain aligned with how our products, systems, and partner relationships operate.

- Lead trading operations readiness for regulatory exams, audits, and internal testing, including producing operational evidence, supporting responses, remediating findings, and translating identified gaps into sustainable process or system improvements.

- Manage day-to-day operational relationships with our carrying broker, executing brokers, custodians, fund companies, and transfer agents, including escalations, service-level performance, issue resolution, and operational change management.

- Partner closely with Product and Engineering on system-managed trading workflows and controls, bringing the operational and supervisory perspective to requirements, pressure-testing exceptions and edge cases, and ensuring appropriate operational readiness and oversight before launch, including post-launch operational testing to confirm controls perform as designed in production.

- Build the reporting and operational visibility needed to oversee the trading function, including volumes, breaks and errors, aging exceptions, settlement performance, and control effectiveness, using those insights to identify risk, capacity constraints, and opportunities for improvement.

- Partner with Compliance, Finance, Legal, Risk, Product, and Engineering on new products, partners, and regulatory changes, defining the trading operations and supervisory requirements needed to launch and operate them safely.

You should:

- Hold active FINRA Series 7, Series 63, and Series 24 licenses (Series 99 or Series 57 a plus.

- 8+ years in trading, brokerage, or investment operations, including direct ownership of trade lifecycle, settlement, or trading control functions.

- Have hands-on operational experience across fixed income, mutual funds, and ETFs — you know where each product breaks and why.

- Have built or materially improved a trade surveillance or operational control framework, not just executed someone else’s.

- Possess a strong working knowledge of the operational requirements under FINRA and SEC rules — including recordkeeping, supervision, best execution, trade reporting, and customer protection — and know how to apply them to workflows that don’t have an obvious precedent.

- Communicate clearly in writing — procedures, escalations, and post-mortems that a regulator, an engineer, and an executive can each read and act on.

- Be comfortable operating in ambiguity and at speed, and be willing to design the process rather than wait for one.

- Bring judgment about when to automate, when to add a control, and when to accept a manual step — and be able to defend the call.

Nice to have:

- Experience at a fintech or high-growth firm operating a broker-dealer or RIA at scale.

- Experience standing up a new product, partner, or clearing relationships from scratch.

- Comfort with SQL or working directly in internal tooling to investigate issues yourself.

jobs.title: Treasury Operations Analyst
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
Role Overview:

We're looking for a hands-on Treasury Operations Analyst to own the day-to-day execution of Mercury's cash management and reporting processes. This is an execution- and build-focused role: you'll manage cash movements and approvals, maintain Treasury's core reporting cadence, and — critically — design and build the automated tools and workflows that let Treasury operate without relying on manual spreadsheet work or costly third-party platforms.

We're especially interested in candidates who are fluent with modern AI and prioritize process and reporting automations. If you've automated processes to gain scale and efficiency we want to hear about it.

Cash Management & Operations:

- Execute and approve daily cash movements across Mercury's accounts, ensuring accuracy, proper authorization, and timely settlement

- Maintain daily cash positioning and reporting, tracking balances across operating, reserve, and partner bank accounts

- Manage reserve account funding across Mercury's partner bank relationships, ensuring balances comply with contractual requirements and reconciling reserve calculations against underlying agreements

- Support cash forecasting by maintaining and refreshing short-term cash flow models

- Own bank account access and rights administration

Reporting & Automation (Build Focus):

- Design, build, and maintain automated cash and liquidity reporting — reducing reliance on manual spreadsheet processes and off-the-shelf treasury management tooling

- Build scalable tools for cash positioning, reserve tracking, and reporting workflows

- Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reporting packages (e.g., ALCO materials, deposit summaries, liquidity metrics)

- Own data pulls and validation from internal systems (e.g., NetSuite, Snowflake) to support reporting accuracy

- Continuously look for manual, error-prone, or repetitive Treasury processes and propose/build automated replacements

Cross-Functional Support:

- Partner with Accounting to ensure cash activity, reserve movements, and facility transactions are properly reflected in the GL

- Work with Data/Analytics teams to acquire cash data feeds from third-party banks to support Treasury and broader Finance reporting

- Support ALCO and management reporting with accurate, well-formatted, timely inputs

- Assist with ad hoc requests from the Treasurer and broader Finance team

What We're Looking For:

- Prior experience at a fintech, bank, or other regulated financial institution

- 2–5 years of experience in treasury operations, corporate treasury, FP&A, or a related finance/accounting function

- High attention to detail — this role involves approving real money movements and compliance-sensitive reporting

- Strong data modeling skills; comfort with large datasets

- Demonstrated experience thoughtfully transitioning manual processes to scalable automations to gain efficiencies

- Familiarity with SQL and/or willingness to learn (Snowflake, Omni experience a plus)

- Exposure to NetSuite or similar ERP/GL systems a plus

- Strong written communication; comfortable producing clean, concise reporting for senior stakeholders and external counterparties (third-party banks, lenders)

- Self-starter comfortable in an ambiguous, build-as-you-go environment

- Experience using AI tools to prototype automated processes

Nice to Have:

- Experience with partner bank / BaaS reserve account structures

- Prior use of Treasury Management Systems

- Familiarity with deposit sweep networks

- Experience supporting Federal Reserve account operations

- Project management skills — this role will involve owning trackers and multi-workstream initiatives

We work hard to create the easiest and safest banking* experience possible to simplify our customer’s financial lives whether they are entrepreneurs, business owners, or individuals.  Mercury has also obtained a provisional national bank charter and is currently taking proactive steps for final approval.

We're looking for a Business Risk Officer to help scale the way Mercury builds products.  In this role you will report to our Head of Business Risk & Enablement and will partner with Product, Operations, Compliance and many other support and oversight teams to ensure that products and features are delivered “best-in-class” in a safe and sound manner.  Your success in this role will rely on subject matter expertise in one or more of Mercury’s core product offerings and associated risks. You will also be primarily responsible for the facilitation of non-financial risk management programs (see below).

- Identify any potential blind spots in processes and controls, and suggest commercial improvements/enhancements

- Facilitate pre-launch and new activity initiatives/reviews, tracking items to closure and escalating where/when necessary

- Facilitate execution of risk self assessments and similar exercises within the non-financial risk frameworks

- Event/incident, issues , and remediations management - ensuring that incidents and issues are recorded and managed through to remediation in line with any and all relevant frameworks in the company

- Excellent communication skills to simplify complex business, reg and/or risk concepts into clear explanations and/or recommendations

- Familiarity with Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) practices and non-financial risk frameworks

jobs.title: Lead Compliance Risk Manager, Product Compliance - AI
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the role:

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly.

Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years.

We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.

We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.

How this role fits alongside our other AI roles : this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program.

In this role, you will:

- Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.

-

- Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.

- Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.

- Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.

- Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.

- Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.

- Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.

- Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.

Core responsibilities:

- Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.

- Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.

- Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.

- Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.

- Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.

- Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.

- Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.

- Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.

- Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.

- Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.

- Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.

- Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.

You should have :

- 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.

- Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.

- Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.

- Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.

- Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.

- Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.

- Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.

- Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.

- Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.

- Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate regulatory and financial partner risk into terms stakeholder teams understand, and to resolve conflict around risk tolerance, resourcing, and timelines.

- Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.

- Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.

- Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the Team

Transaction Risk Enablement is the shared services function supporting Mercury's Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX programs. We build the knowledge base articles, SOPs, and eLearning that frontline teams rely on to do their jobs accurately and consistently — and that hold up to regulatory scrutiny in a financial services environment. This is a small, high-output team doing work that directly shapes how well-documented and audit-ready Mercury's risk operations are.

Role Summary

We're looking for a L&D Specialist to join a growing team supporting Fraud, Disputes, and Risk UX. You'll write and maintain formal SOPs, Guru knowledge base articles, and Articulate-built eLearning — translating operational processes and regulatory requirements into content that's clear, accurate, and usable by the teams who rely on it every day. You'll work primarily within one or two of these domains, going deep on the processes and regulatory context that matter most there, while collaborating with Specialists and SMEs across the broader team.

This is an experienced-contributor role: you'll own content projects from scoping through publication with minimal oversight, exercise sound judgment in ambiguous or incomplete-information situations, and be looked to as a source of regulatory and process knowledge others build on. You're not just executing a content backlog — you're expected to spot where standards or resources need to improve and drive those improvements yourself.

This is a strong fit for someone who enjoys both the craft of instructional design and the discipline of regulatory-grade technical writing — and who wants ownership over content that has real operational weight, not just training that gets built once and forgotten.

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

- Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.

- Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.

- Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.

- Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.

- Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.

- Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.

- Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.

- Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.

- Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.

- Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.

- Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.

- Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.

- Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.

- Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

- 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development,  quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.

- Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.

- Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.

- Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.

- Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.

- Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.

- Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.

- High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred qualifications:

- Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.

- Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.

- Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:

- Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.

- Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.

- Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.

- Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.

- Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

In Rome, senators were barred from shipping grain for profit. In India, Buddhist parables warned of merchants who abused their customers’ trust. Where there is innovation, there must also be controls ensuring a strong, trustworthy foundation upon which the growth is built.

At Mercury, we believe compliance is the infrastructure of trust—a way to engineer safety, transparency, and integrity directly into the architecture of financial innovation. This isn’t about bureaucracy or backstops. It’s about building control systems that scale with ambition, that evolve with product velocity, and that speak fluently in the language of risk and regulation.

We’re hiring a Senior Compliance Risk Manager, Securities to help us continue this tradition: someone who can translate regulation into design, design into process, and process into enduring trust. The Senior Compliance Risk Manager will independently execute on our securities compliance and supervision program while driving high-quality oversight across regulated entities, marketing programs, and financial partnership projects. This role bridges tactical execution with strategic ownership, providing operational clarity and regulatory confidence in how Mercury builds and scales.

This role is well-suited for someone who thrives on execution, is energized by precision, and enjoys cross-functional problem-solving. Responsibilities will span a wide range of areas, from conducting compliance testing and inspections, owning annual completion and certification of compliance reports, maintaining policy and procedure inventory, supporting regulatory investigations and examinations, licensing, surveillance, marketing, and regulatory filings. The Strategic Partnerships team drives customer growth, product expansion, and strategic advantage through high-impact partner relationships. We build and manage partnerships across the startup ecosystem: accounting firms, VCs, investors, ecommerce partners, incorporators, platforms, and financial institutions.
